scenario: Over coffee the team plays 'what might have been', reflecting on choices — so the episode features mixed conditionals (past condition → present result, and vice versa), wish + past perfect, and a little formal inversion. Kate: 'If I hadn't joined this company, I wouldn't be sitting here with you now.' Den: 'If Valery hadn't retired, he'd still be grumbling in that corner.' Pol: 'If I were more organised, I would have finished the report yesterday.' Alex: 'Had we left ten minutes earlier that day, we wouldn't have been stuck in the lift.' Peter: 'I wish I had learned to code sooner.' It stays warm and hopeful — nobody really regrets anything; they're glad how things turned out. Use clearly: mixed conditionals ('If + past perfect, would + verb now' and 'If + past simple, would have + V3'), 'wish/if only + past perfect', and one or two inverted conditionals ('Had I known...'). B2, sentences crisp not sprawling.
